options.A: CRP does not tend to correlate with anti-dsDNA or complement
options.B: CRP falls whenever anti-dsDNA rises, in a fixed ratio
options.C: Complement and CRP always move together
options.E: The paper says CRP replaces complement testing

mcqs.correctAnswerText: CRP does not tend to correlate with anti-dsDNA or complement
mcqs.explanation: CRP levels do not tend to correlate with anti-dsDNA antibodies or complement levels.

sourceRefs.excerpt: CRP levels do not tend to correlate with other markers of disease activity such as anti-double stranded DNA antibodies and complement levels

mcqs.question: Which CRP threshold has been associated with infection in SLE in the studies this paper cites?

options.A: CRP greater than 6.0 mg/dl
options.B: CRP less than 0.1 mg/dl
options.D: CRP is never raised in infection
options.E: Only ESR, not CRP, has been linked to infection

mcqs.correctAnswerText: CRP greater than 6.0 mg/dl
mcqs.explanation: CRP values above 6.0 mg/dl in SLE have been associated with infectious processes in several studies, and CRP is higher in infection than in flare without infection.

sourceRefs.excerpt: CRP values of >6.0 mg/dl in SLE patients have been associated with infectious processes in several studies

mcqs.question: In this series, which ESR:CRP ratios pointed toward infection versus flare?

options.A: Infection predominated at ≤2 and flare at ≥15
options.B: Flare predominated at ≤2 and infection at ≥15
options.E: A ratio of 2 diagnosed lupus nephritis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Infection predominated at ≤2 and flare at ≥15
mcqs.explanation: Infections predominated when the ESR:CRP ratio was 2 or lower, and flares predominated at ratios of 15 or higher.

sourceRefs.excerpt: infections predominant for ratios of ≤2, and flares predominant for ratios of ≥15; p<0.000

mcqs.question: Which flare features were associated with higher CRP?

options.A: Serosal flares had higher CRP than flares without serositis
options.B: Arthritis flares had the highest CRP in every comparison
options.D: Myositis flares had undetectable CRP by definition
options.E: CRP was identical in all flare types

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Serosal flares had higher CRP than flares without serositis
mcqs.explanation: The 10 flares with a serosal component had higher CRP than the 18 without (8.7±8.3 versus 3.6±4.6, p=0.04).

sourceRefs.excerpt: CRP levels were higher for the 10 flares with a serosal component compared to the 18 flares without a serosal component [8.7 ±8.3 vs 3.6 ±4.6 (p=0.04)

mcqs.question: Why do the authors say a flare-versus-infection distinction matters before immunosuppression?

options.A: High-dose glucocorticoids and other immunosuppression can be dangerous if the process is infection
options.B: Immunosuppression treats bacterial infection
options.E: ESR must be normalized before any culture

mcqs.correctAnswerText: High-dose glucocorticoids and other immunosuppression can be dangerous if the process is infection
mcqs.explanation: Presumptive flare treatment with immunosuppressants, including high-dose glucocorticoids, can be dangerous if infection is present, so aggressive immunosuppression is usually postponed until infection is excluded.

sourceRefs.excerpt: presumptive treatment of SLE flares with immunosuppressive medications, including high dose glucocorticoids, can be dangerous in the setting of an infection

topics.topicDisplayName: SLE: SLICC 2012 and ACR/EULAR 2019 classification criteria compared
topics.coverageNote: Direct comparison of the 2019 structure with SLICC 2012 and ACR 1997. The SLICC derivation paper alone cannot describe the 2019 criteria.

mcqs.question: What immunologic rule did SLICC 2012 add, as summarized in the 2019 paper?

options.A: At least one immunologic criterion is required, and histology-compatible nephritis plus ANA or anti-dsDNA is sufficient to classify SLE
options.B: ANA must be negative
options.C: Four clinical criteria and no antibodies
options.D: Anti-Sm is mandatory in every case
options.E: Nephritis excludes classification

mcqs.correctAnswerText: At least one immunologic criterion is required, and histology-compatible nephritis plus ANA or anti-dsDNA is sufficient to classify SLE
mcqs.explanation: SLICC required at least one immunologic criterion and allowed histology-proven compatible nephritis plus ANA or anti-dsDNA to classify SLE.

sourceRefs.excerpt: requiring at least one immunological criterion to be present, and categorized histology-proven nephritis compatible with SLE as sufficient for classification, if anti-nuclear antibodies (ANA) or antibodies to double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) were present.

mcqs.question: How did SLICC sensitivity and specificity compare with the 1997 ACR criteria?

options.A: Higher sensitivity and lower specificity
options.B: Lower sensitivity and higher specificity
options.C: Both sensitivity and specificity were higher
options.E: Specificity was not compared

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Higher sensitivity and lower specificity
mcqs.explanation: SLICC increased sensitivity and had lower specificity than the 1997 ACR criteria.

sourceRefs.excerpt: While achieving their goal of increasing sensitivity, the SLICC criteria have lower specificity than the 1997 ACR criteria

mcqs.question: Why did the 2019 criteria use a positive ANA as an entry criterion?

options.A: ANA has high sensitivity and limited specificity, and the structure was thought to reflect SLE pathogenesis
options.B: ANA has perfect specificity
options.C: ANA-negative SLE is the most common subset
options.E: Entry criteria were rejected

mcqs.correctAnswerText: ANA has high sensitivity and limited specificity, and the structure was thought to reflect SLE pathogenesis
mcqs.explanation: A positive ANA entry criterion was chosen to reflect pathogenesis and ANA's high sensitivity with limited specificity.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Such an approach was thought to reflect underlying SLE pathogenesis, and take into account ANA test characteristics of high sensitivity and limited specificity.

mcqs.question: Why were 2019 criteria weighted rather than counted equally?

options.A: Items are not equally useful; mucosal ulcers and biopsy-proven nephritis were the example given
options.B: Weights were required by regulators and have no clinical meaning
options.C: Every item has the same weight by design
options.E: Weighting was tried and abandoned

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Items are not equally useful; mucosal ulcers and biopsy-proven nephritis were the example given
mcqs.explanation: Individual criteria were not expected to be equally useful, for example mucosal ulcers versus biopsy-proven lupus nephritis, so weighted criteria were developed.

sourceRefs.excerpt: we expected individual criteria would not be of equal utility (weight) for the classification of

mcqs.question: In whom do existing SLE classification criteria perform better, according to this paper?

options.A: Longstanding disease more than new-onset SLE
options.B: New-onset disease more than longstanding disease
options.E: Performance does not vary by disease duration

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Longstanding disease more than new-onset SLE
mcqs.explanation: Existing criteria perform better in longstanding disease than in new-onset SLE, which is why the 2019 project enriched samples for early disease.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Existing SLE classification criteria perform better in patients with longstanding disease than in new-onset SLE

topics.topicDisplayName: Scleroderma ILD: HRCT patterns, nintedanib, mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide
topics.coverageNote: HRCT is the diagnostic standard in the cited consensus. Pattern-subtype frequencies are not invented.

mcqs.question: What is the primary diagnostic tool for systemic-sclerosis ILD in the European consensus this paper cites?

options.A: Chest HRCT, supported by pulmonary function tests
options.B: Chest radiograph alone
options.D: Bronchoscopy in every patient before any imaging
options.E: Six-minute-walk distance alone

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Chest HRCT, supported by pulmonary function tests
mcqs.explanation: Chest HRCT is the primary diagnostic tool, supported by PFTs for screening and diagnosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) as the primary diagnostic tool for SSc-ILD, supported by pulmonary function tests (PFTs) for screening and diagnosis

mcqs.question: Which lung-function changes suggest progression?

options.A: Declining FVC and DLCO
options.B: Rising FEV1/FVC only
options.C: A single normal DLCO excludes progression forever
options.E: The paper says PFTs are not useful

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Declining FVC and DLCO
mcqs.explanation: Declining FVC and DLCO can suggest progression of ILD.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Declining values for forced vital capacity (FVC) and diffusing capacity of the lungs for carbon monoxide (DL CO ) can suggest progression of ILD

mcqs.question: How does mycophenolate compare with cyclophosphamide?

options.A: Similar efficacy and less toxicity
options.B: Clearly less effective and more toxic
options.D: It is used only after transplant
options.E: It replaces nintedanib because SENSCIS was negative

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Similar efficacy and less toxicity
mcqs.explanation: Mycophenolate mofetil provides similar efficacy to cyclophosphamide and is associated with less toxicity. EULAR is cited as recommending cyclophosphamide for systemic-sclerosis ILD.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Mycophenolate mofetil (MMF) provides similar efficacy to CYC and is associated with less toxicity

mcqs.question: On which trial is nintedanib's approval for systemic-sclerosis ILD based?

options.A: SENSCIS
options.B: TEAR
options.E: MAINRITSAN

mcqs.correctAnswerText: SENSCIS
mcqs.explanation: Nintedanib is approved for systemic-sclerosis ILD based on SENSCIS, and for progressive fibrosing ILDs based on INBUILD.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Nintedanib has been approved for the treatment of SSc-ILD and chronic fibrosing ILDs with a progressive phenotype based on the results of the SENSCIS and INBUILD trials respectively

mcqs.question: When may hematopoietic stem-cell transplantation be considered, and what risk does the paper emphasize?

options.A: Rapidly progressive systemic sclerosis at risk of organ failure, with a high risk of treatment-related side effects and death
options.B: Every patient with stable limited cutaneous disease
options.D: Only after nintedanib has failed for 10 years
options.E: It has no stated risk

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Rapidly progressive systemic sclerosis at risk of organ failure, with a high risk of treatment-related side effects and death
mcqs.explanation: Transplant may be considered for rapidly progressive disease at risk of organ failure, but patients must be selected carefully because of a high risk of treatment-related side effects and mortality.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Hematopoietic stem cell transplantation may also be considered in patients with rapidly progressive SSc at risk of organ failure, although careful selection of patients is required due to a high risk of treatment-related side effects and mortality

topics.topicDisplayName: Scleroderma Renal Crisis
topics.coverageNote: Same open update is used for catalogue 1510. UKSSG 2015 was not the open full text retrieved.

mcqs.question: What classical presentation defines scleroderma renal crisis in this update?

options.A: Accelerated hypertension and creatinine rising to more than 1.5 times baseline
options.B: Isolated microscopic hematuria with normal blood pressure
options.D: Chronic kidney disease developing over years without a blood-pressure change
options.E: Pulmonary hemorrhage as the required feature

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Accelerated hypertension and creatinine rising to more than 1.5 times baseline
mcqs.explanation: Renal crisis classically presents with accelerated hypertension and AKI defined as serum creatinine more than 1.5 times baseline.

sourceRefs.excerpt: SRC classically presents with accelerated hypertension and acute kidney injury (AKI) defined as an increase in serum creatinine > 1.5 × baseline.

mcqs.question: Which other renal diseases does the update say belong in the differential?

options.A: ANCA-associated vasculitis, membranous nephropathy, and thrombotic microangiopathies
options.B: Only diabetic nephropathy
options.C: IgA nephropathy is the only mimic
options.D: No differential is needed once hypertension is present
options.E: Multiple myeloma only

mcqs.correctAnswerText: ANCA-associated vasculitis, membranous nephropathy, and thrombotic microangiopathies
mcqs.explanation: ANCA vasculitis, membranous nephritis, and thrombotic microangiopathies such as TTP or DIC are listed among causes to consider.

sourceRefs.excerpt: other causes to consider include anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA)–associated vasculitis, membranous nephritis, other primary causes of thrombotic microangiopathies

mcqs.question: What historical change does the update credit with reducing mortality?

options.A: Introduction of ACE inhibitors in the 1980s
options.B: Routine bilateral nephrectomy
options.E: Plasma exchange for every patient

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Introduction of ACE inhibitors in the 1980s
mcqs.explanation: Mortality fell significantly after ACE inhibitors were introduced in the 1980s. Earlier treatment had been antihypertensives such as methyldopa or propranolol, dialysis, and sometimes bilateral nephrectomy.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Mortality significantly reduced with the introduction of ACEi in the 1980s

mcqs.question: How quickly should an ACE inhibitor be started once renal crisis is suspected?

options.A: Immediately
options.B: After a week of observation
options.E: ACE inhibitors are contraindicated

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Immediately
mcqs.explanation: An ACE inhibitor should be started immediately if scleroderma renal crisis is suspected.

sourceRefs.excerpt: An ACEi should be started immediately if SRC suspected

mcqs.question: If creatinine keeps rising after blood pressure is controlled on an ACE inhibitor, what should be done?

options.A: The rise should not prompt stopping the ACE inhibitor
options.B: Stop the ACE inhibitor the same day
options.C: Switch immediately to a calcium-channel blocker and never restart an ACE inhibitor
options.D: The rise proves the diagnosis was wrong
options.E: Add an ARB and stop the ACE inhibitor

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The rise should not prompt stopping the ACE inhibitor
mcqs.explanation: Renal function can continue to deteriorate despite the ACE inhibitor and blood-pressure correction, and that should not prompt the drug to be stopped.

sourceRefs.excerpt: renal function can continue to deteriorate despite initiation of ACEi and correction of blood pressure. This should not promp

topics.topicDisplayName: Scleroderma renal crisis: ACE inhibitors, hypertensive emergency, captopril
topics.coverageNote: Questions are limited to ACE-inhibitor choice, titration, and pregnancy.

mcqs.question: Which ACE inhibitor does the update prefer in pregnancy, and why?

options.A: Captopril, because of a lower risk of fetal renal complications
options.B: Ramipril, because it is long-acting and non-teratogenic
options.C: Enalapril, as the only ACE inhibitor studied
options.D: No ACE inhibitor may be used in pregnancy even if the mother is dying
options.E: Losartan is preferred to any ACE inhibitor

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Captopril, because of a lower risk of fetal renal complications
mcqs.explanation: In pregnancy, captopril is preferred because of a lower risk of fetal renal complications. The teratogenic risk is outweighed by the threat of renal crisis to the mother.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Captopril is the preferred choice due to lower risk of foetal renal complications. ACEi carries a teratogenic risk to the foetus but in this scenario, this is outweighed by the life-threatening complication of SRC to the mother.

mcqs.question: Which ACE inhibitor is most often used, and when is captopril suitable outside pregnancy?

options.A: A long-acting agent such as ramipril is most used; captopril may suit hemodynamic compromise
options.B: Captopril is mandatory in every outpatient
options.E: ACE inhibitors are interchangeable with beta-blockers as first-line

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A long-acting agent such as ramipril is most used; captopril may suit hemodynamic compromise
mcqs.explanation: A long-acting ACE inhibitor such as ramipril is most used, but short-acting captopril may be suitable when there is hemodynamic compromise.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A long-acting ACEi such as ramipril is most used but short-acting agents such as captopril may be suitable in cases of haemodynamic compromise.

mcqs.question: How is a long-acting ACE inhibitor titrated?

options.A: The dose is normally doubled at about 24-hour intervals
options.B: The dose is fixed and never increased
options.C: It is doubled every 15 minutes until creatinine normalizes
options.E: It is reduced by half each day

mcqs.correctAnswerText: The dose is normally doubled at about 24-hour intervals
mcqs.explanation: A long-acting agent is doubled at 24-hour intervals up toward the maximum dose. Adequate blood-pressure control often takes 3–5 days.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A long-acting agent is preferable in most cases as it can be easily up-titrated to maximum dose, normally by doubling the dose at 24-h intervals. Adequate control of blood pressure often takes 3–5 days.

mcqs.question: A patient with prior renal crisis is planning pregnancy. What does the update recommend about the ACE inhibitor?

options.A: Continue the ACE inhibitor during pregnancy and optimize blood pressure before conception
options.B: Stop it three months before conception in every case
options.D: Pregnancy is impossible after renal crisis
options.E: Continue it only in the third trimester

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Continue the ACE inhibitor during pregnancy and optimize blood pressure before conception
mcqs.explanation: For patients with a history of renal crisis who are planning pregnancy, the ACE inhibitor should continue and blood pressure should be optimized before conception, acknowledging teratogenic risk.

sourceRefs.excerpt: In patients with history of SRC planning a pregnancy, it is recommended that ACEi continue during the pregnancy and BP is optimised prior to conceiving.

mcqs.question: If the patient is already on an ACE inhibitor when crisis is recognized, what is the next dose change?

options.A: Increase the dose
options.B: Stop it because it caused the crisis
options.D: Replace it with methyldopa as in historical practice
options.E: No change until biopsy

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Increase the dose
mcqs.explanation: If the patient is already taking an ACE inhibitor, the dose should be increased.

sourceRefs.excerpt: If the patient is already taking an ACEi, then the dose should be increased.

topics.topicDisplayName: Septic Arthritis
topics.coverageNote: Native-joint septic arthritis guideline. Prosthetic-joint papers were not used.

mcqs.question: What is the basis of diagnosis in the SANJO guideline?

options.A: Aspiration of joint fluid, with bacterial identification the most important analysis
options.B: Serum CRP alone
options.D: Blood culture without sampling the joint
options.E: Clinical redness without fluid analysis

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Aspiration of joint fluid, with bacterial identification the most important analysis
mcqs.explanation: Diagnosis is based mainly on joint-fluid aspiration. The fluid is analyzed for leucocyte count, but bacterial identification is most important.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The diagnosis of septic arthritis in native joints (SANJO) is mainly based on aspiration of joint fluid, which initially is analysed for synovial leucocyte count, but most important, for bacterial identification.

mcqs.question: When may empirical antibiotics start before joint-fluid sampling?

options.A: When the patient has signs of sepsis; otherwise sampling should come first to avoid false-negative cultures
options.B: Always, before any aspiration
options.E: Only if the Gram stain is already negative

mcqs.correctAnswerText: When the patient has signs of sepsis; otherwise sampling should come first to avoid false-negative cultures
mcqs.explanation: Except for patients with signs of sepsis, empirical antibiotics should await diagnostic sampling so cultures are not falsely negative.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Except for patients with signs of sepsis, empirical antibiotic treatment should await diagnostic sampling of joint fluid to avoid false negative culture results.

mcqs.question: Which operation does SANJO recommend, particularly for larger joints?

options.A: Arthroscopic lavage, with synovectomy depending on stage; open revision if there are adhesions or cartilage or bone damage
options.B: Immediate amputation
options.E: Synovectomy of every small joint of the hand

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Arthroscopic lavage, with synovectomy depending on stage; open revision if there are adhesions or cartilage or bone damage
mcqs.explanation: Arthroscopic lavage, with synovectomy depending on clinical stage, is recommended particularly in larger joints. Open revision may be considered for adhesions or cartilage or bone damage.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Arthroscopic lavage (with synovectomy, depending on the clinical stage) is recommended for SANJO particularly in larger joints, although open revision could be considered in cases with synovial membrane adhesions or in the presence of cartilage or bone damage.

mcqs.question: How should empirical antibiotics be chosen and then adjusted?

options.A: Choose them for the most likely pathogens, then target them to microbiology results
options.B: Use a fixed two-week oral course regardless of cultures
options.C: Antibiotics are not recommended if lavage is performed
options.D: Vancomycin is mandatory for every native joint
options.E: Stop antibiotics when the white-cell count falls below 50,000 even if cultures are pending

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Choose them for the most likely pathogens, then target them to microbiology results
mcqs.explanation: Empirical treatment should reflect the most likely pathogens and then be targeted to laboratory results.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Empirical antibiotic treatment should be selected considering the most likely pathogens and targeted according to the results from microbiology laboratory.

mcqs.question: When does SANJO say to start mobilizing the joint?

options.A: As soon as infection is controlled and drains have been removed, to avoid contracture
options.B: On arrival, before antibiotics
options.C: Only after six weeks of splinting
options.E: After the CRP has been normal for 30 days, regardless of drains

mcqs.correctAnswerText: As soon as infection is controlled and drains have been removed, to avoid contracture
mcqs.explanation: Joint mobilization to avoid contracture should start as soon as possible once infection is controlled and drains are out.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Joint mobilization to avoid contracture should be started as soon as possible when infection is under control and after drains have been removed.

topics.topicDisplayName: Septic arthritis: diagnosis, Gram stain, joint aspiration, empirical antibiotics, surgical drainage
topics.coverageNote: Same SANJO guideline, with questions on aspiration timing, Gram stain, and drainage.

mcqs.question: If only a little synovial fluid is obtained, what is the analysis priority?

options.A: Bacterial identification, then white-cell count including PMN percentage, then crystals
options.B: Crystals first, culture last
options.E: The guideline says not to prioritize

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Bacterial identification, then white-cell count including PMN percentage, then crystals
mcqs.explanation: Priority if volume is limited is bacterial identification, white-cell count with PMN percentage, then crystals.

sourceRefs.excerpt: white blood cell count including polymorphonuclear (PMN) percentage, and presence of crystals (in that priority order if the quantity of liquid is not enough

mcqs.question: How should a synovial white-cell count above 50,000 per microlitre be used?

options.A: It suggests septic arthritis but is not sufficient alone
options.B: It confirms septic arthritis without culture
options.E: The guideline does not use a 50,000 threshold

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It suggests septic arthritis but is not sufficient alone
mcqs.explanation: A count above 50,000/µL suggests septic arthritis but alone is not sufficient for the diagnosis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A synovial white blood cell count of > 50 000 cells µ L - 1 is suggestive of SANJO, but alone is not sufficient for the diagnosis

mcqs.question: What does a synovial white-cell count below 25,000 per microlitre mean?

options.A: It decreases the post-test probability but does not exclude septic arthritis
options.B: It excludes infection
options.E: It is the threshold for antibiotics before culture

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It decreases the post-test probability but does not exclude septic arthritis
mcqs.explanation: A count below 25,000/µL lowers post-test probability but cannot exclude septic arthritis. Cut-offs may not apply in immunosuppressed patients.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Low synovial white blood cell count ( < 25 000 cells µ L - 1 ) decreases post-test probability, but it cannot exclude SANJO

mcqs.question: Why perform a Gram stain despite limited sensitivity?

options.A: Specificity is excellent, so a positive stain is early proof of infection and can guide empirical treatment
options.B: Sensitivity is 100%
options.C: A negative stain ends the work-up
options.E: The guideline advises against Gram stain

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Specificity is excellent, so a positive stain is early proof of infection and can guide empirical treatment
mcqs.explanation: Gram stain is recommended despite limited sensitivity because excellent specificity can provide early proof of infection and help guide empirical treatment.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Performing Gram staining on synovial fluid is recommended despite its limited sensitivity; given its excellent specificity, it can provide early proof of infection and help guiding empirical treatment

mcqs.question: How should the remaining fluid be cultured?

options.A: Inoculate blood-culture bottles; also plate sterile-tube fluid on agar and enrichment broth; incubate 5–7 days
options.B: A dry swab of the skin is sufficient
options.C: Culture is optional if the white-cell count is high
options.E: Use viral culture media only

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Inoculate blood-culture bottles; also plate sterile-tube fluid on agar and enrichment broth; incubate 5–7 days
mcqs.explanation: Remaining fluid should go into blood-culture bottles. Sterile-tube fluid should be plated on agar and thioglycolate enrichment broth as well or instead. Incubation of 5–7 days is recommended according to local practice.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Synovial fluid from a sterile tube should be plated on agar plates and enrichment broth (thioglycolate)

topics.topicDisplayName: Shared decision making and patient reported outcomes in rheumatology: HAQ, PROMIS, PROs

options.A: CDAI, DAS28-ESR/CRP, PAS-II, RAPID3, and SDAI
options.B: HAQ, ESR, CRP, rheumatoid factor, and anti-CCP only

mcqs.explanation: Five preferred RA disease-activity measures were selected: CDAI, DAS28-ESR/CRP, PAS-II, RAPID3, and SDAI.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Five preferred RA disease activity measures for regular clinical use were selected: CDAI, DAS28-ESR/CRP, PAS-II, RAPID3, and SDAI.

mcqs.question: Which functional-status instruments does the parallel recommendation name?

options.A: PROMIS Physical Function 10, MD-HAQ, and HAQ-II
options.B: Only the original HAQ, with PROMIS excluded
options.E: No functional measure was recommended

mcqs.correctAnswerText: PROMIS Physical Function 10, MD-HAQ, and HAQ-II
mcqs.explanation: Functional-status recommendations include PROMIS Physical Function 10, the Multi-Dimensional HAQ, and HAQ-II.

sourceRefs.excerpt: recommendations for the use of PROMIS Physical Function 10, MD-HAQ, and HAQ-II

mcqs.question: Where do the HAQ and the MDHAQ sit inside the preferred disease-activity indices named here?

options.A: PAS contains the HAQ, and RAPID3 contains the MDHAQ
options.B: CDAI is composed only of the HAQ
options.C: SDAI replaces both questionnaires with CRP
options.D: DAS28 contains the full HAQ disability index
options.E: Neither questionnaire is used in any preferred index

mcqs.correctAnswerText: PAS contains the HAQ, and RAPID3 contains the MDHAQ
mcqs.explanation: PAS contains the Health Assessment Questionnaire, and RAPID3 contains the Multi-Dimensional Health Assessment Questionnaire.

sourceRefs.excerpt: PAS contains the Health Assessment Questionnaire ( ) and RAPID3 contains the MultiDimensional Health Assessment Questionnaire (MDHAQ)

mcqs.question: What does the update say about disease-activity scores that include patient-reported measures when fibromyalgia is also present?

options.A: Those scores are higher in patients with comorbid fibromyalgia
options.B: Those scores fall to zero
options.C: Fibromyalgia does not change any patient-reported score
options.D: Only laboratory-based scores rise, and patient-reported scores fall
options.E: The update says fibromyalgia invalidates the CDAI but not RAPID3

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Those scores are higher in patients with comorbid fibromyalgia
mcqs.explanation: Disease-activity scores that include patient-reported measures are higher in patients with comorbid fibromyalgia.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Disease activity scores including patient reported measures are higher in patients with comorbid fibromyalgia

mcqs.question: What does this update actually recommend a clinician do when putting a measure into routine use?

options.A: Select one preferred measure (CDAI, DAS28, PAS-II, RAPID3, or SDAI), without precluding other measures
options.B: Use every preferred measure at every visit
options.C: Replace disease-activity measurement with a shared-decision checklist that this paper defines
options.E: Use imaging as the only regular measure

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Select one preferred measure (CDAI, DAS28, PAS-II, RAPID3, or SDAI), without precluding other measures
mcqs.explanation: When integrating measurement into the record, the update recommends selecting a preferred measure and does not preclude other RA disease-activity measures. It does not define a shared-decision procedure.

topics.topicDisplayName: Sjogren syndrome: sicca symptoms, anti-Ro, anti-La, MALT lymphoma risk, systemic features

mcqs.question: How does this review characterize Sjögren disease at the outset?

options.A: A systemic autoimmune disorder with hypofunction of the salivary and lacrimal glands

sourceRefs.excerpt: Sjögren’s disease is a systemic autoimmune disorder characterized by hypofunction of salivary and lacrimal glands

mcqs.question: What does the review say about anti-SSA/Ro antibodies?

options.A: They are present in nearly 75% of patients and play a key role in diagnosis
options.B: They are present in fewer than 5% and exclude the diagnosis
options.C: They are identical to rheumatoid factor

options.E: They have no diagnostic role

mcqs.correctAnswerText: They are present in nearly 75% of patients and play a key role in diagnosis
mcqs.explanation: Anti-SSA/Ro antibodies are present in nearly 75% of patients with Sjögren disease and play a key role in diagnosis.

mcqs.question: Which antibody finding was associated with increased mortality in the studies this review cites, along with older age and male sex?

options.A: Anti-La/SSB positivity
options.B: Anti-CCP positivity

mcqs.explanation: Participants who started on methotrexate stepped up to etanercept, or to sulfasalazine plus hydroxychloroquine, if DAS28-ESR was at least 3.2 at week 24.

sourceRefs.excerpt: initial MTX, with step-up treatment adding ETN if DAS28-ESR was ≥ 3.2 at week 24

mcqs.question: What was the primary comparison of etanercept plus methotrexate versus oral triple therapy?

options.A: No difference between the two treatment approaches
options.B: Etanercept was superior on the primary outcome
options.C: Triple therapy was superior on the primary outcome
options.D: The primary outcome could not be analysed
options.E: Methotrexate monotherapy was superior to both combinations

mcqs.correctAnswerText: No difference between the two treatment approaches
mcqs.explanation: TEAR is described as the only randomized double-blind comparison of oral triple DMARD therapy with etanercept plus methotrexate, and the primary outcome revealed no difference between the two approaches.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The primary outcome revealed no differences between the two treatment approaches.

mcqs.question: Which week-102 difference does the paper report as the only significant treatment difference?

options.A: ACR70 of 18.2% with etanercept versus 11.3% with triple therapy (p=0.02)
options.B: A large DAS28 difference favouring triple therapy
options.C: Modified HAQ was worse with etanercept
options.D: Radiographic remission only in the placebo arm
options.E: No week-102 comparison was statistically significant

mcqs.correctAnswerText: ACR70 of 18.2% with etanercept versus 11.3% with triple therapy (p=0.02)
mcqs.explanation: The only significant treatment difference at week 102 was ACR70, 18.2% in the etanercept group versus 11.3% in the triple-therapy group (p=0.02). Function improved similarly across groups.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the only significant treatment difference at week 102 was between the ETN and triple therapy groups for ACR70 (18.2% vs. 11.3%, p=0.02).

topics.topicDisplayName: Cardiac tamponade: Beck's triad, pericardiocentesis, surgical drainage
topics.coverageNote: ESC 2015 tamponade section. Beck's triad is not named in the text; the listed signs are used instead. A stored 2024 pericardial-imaging statement did not discuss tamponade.

mcqs.question: How does the 2015 ESC guideline define cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Life-threatening compression of the heart by pericardial fluid, pus, blood, clot, or gas
options.B: Any pericardial effusion, regardless of haemodynamic effect
options.C: Constriction of a thickened pericardium without effusion
options.E: Electrical alternans without effusion

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Life-threatening compression of the heart by pericardial fluid, pus, blood, clot, or gas
mcqs.explanation: Cardiac tamponade is life-threatening slow or rapid compression of the heart due to pericardial accumulation of fluid, pus, blood, clots, or gas.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Cardiac tamponade is a life-threatening, slow or rapid compression of the heart due to the pericardial accumulation of fluid, pus, blood, clots or gas

mcqs.question: Which clinical signs does the guideline list?

options.A: Tachycardia, hypotension, pulsus paradoxus, raised jugular venous pressure, and muffled heart sounds
options.B: Fever, splinter haemorrhages, and a new murmur
options.C: Bradycardia, hypertension, and a loud first heart sound
options.E: Only a normal examination with a large effusion on CT

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Tachycardia, hypotension, pulsus paradoxus, raised jugular venous pressure, and muffled heart sounds
mcqs.explanation: The guideline lists tachycardia, hypotension, pulsus paradoxus, raised jugular venous pressure, muffled heart sounds, low voltage with electrical alternans, and an enlarged silhouette when accumulation is slow. It does not name Beck's triad.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Clinical signs in a patient with cardiac tamponade include tachycardia, hypotension, pulsus paradoxus, raised jugular venous pressure, muffled heart sounds

mcqs.question: What is the guideline's definition of pulsus paradoxus?

options.A: An inspiratory decrease in systolic arterial pressure of more than 10 mmHg during normal breathing
options.B: A rise in systolic pressure during inspiration
options.C: Absence of the radial pulse for one minute
options.E: A pericardial rub

mcqs.correctAnswerText: An inspiratory decrease in systolic arterial pressure of more than 10 mmHg during normal breathing
mcqs.explanation: Pulsus paradoxus is conventionally an inspiratory decrease in systolic arterial pressure of more than 10 mmHg during normal breathing. The guideline calls it a key diagnostic finding.

sourceRefs.excerpt: pulsus paradoxus (conventionally defined as an inspiratory decrease in systolic arterial pressure of >10 mmHg during normal breathing)

mcqs.question: Which test does the guideline call the single most useful diagnostic tool, and what procedure does it also guide?

options.A: Echocardiography, which also guides pericardiocentesis
options.B: Chest radiograph alone
options.E: ECG, which replaces drainage

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Echocardiography, which also guides pericardiocentesis
mcqs.explanation: Echocardiography is the single most useful diagnostic tool to identify the effusion and estimate its haemodynamic impact, and it is used to guide pericardiocentesis.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Echocardiography is the single most useful diagnostic tool to identify pericardial effusion and estimate its size, location and degree of haemodynamic impact

mcqs.question: How should tamponade be drained?

options.A: Preferably needle pericardiocentesis with echo or fluoroscopic guidance, without delay if unstable; surgery especially for purulent pericarditis or bleeding
options.B: Oral colchicine as the definitive drainage method
options.D: Pericardiectomy as the first step for every free-flowing effusion
options.E: Needle drainage is contraindicated

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Preferably needle pericardiocentesis with echo or fluoroscopic guidance, without delay if unstable; surgery especially for purulent pericarditis or bleeding
mcqs.explanation: Drainage is preferably by needle pericardiocentesis with echocardiographic or fluoroscopic guidance and should not be delayed in unstable patients. Surgery is the alternative especially for purulent pericarditis or bleeding into the pericardium.

sourceRefs.excerpt: preferably by needle pericardiocentesis, with the use of echocardiographic or fluoroscopic guidance, and should be performed without delay in unstable patients. Alternatively, drainage is performed by a surgical approach, especially in some situations such as purulent pericarditis or in urgent situations with bleeding into the pericardium

topics.topicDisplayName: Meniere's disease: intratympanic therapy, low-salt diet, surgical options
topics.coverageNote: Covers sodium restriction, intratympanic steroid, endolymphatic surgery, and destructive surgery for Ménière disease. A stored BPPV document was not used.

mcqs.question: What does this review say about dietary sodium restriction?

options.A: It has been widely used since 1931, but controlled studies using modern definitions are lacking, and some advocate moderate rather than harsh restriction
options.B: A randomised trial in this paper proves harsh restriction stops all spells
options.D: It was introduced after gentamicin and is first-line destructive therapy
options.E: The review does not discuss diet

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It has been widely used since 1931, but controlled studies using modern definitions are lacking, and some advocate moderate rather than harsh restriction
mcqs.explanation: Sodium restriction has been widely used since 1931. Reduction of dietary sodium plus diuretics has been reported to slow hearing-loss progression. Some advocate moderate regulation rather than harsh restriction, and controlled studies using modern definitions are lacking.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Sodium restriction This has been widely used to control symptoms of Ménière’s disease since 1931.

mcqs.question: Which diuretic combination does the review call the most commonly used medical treatment?

options.A: Hydrochlorothiazide plus triamterene
options.B: Spironolactone as the only diuretic ever used
options.C: Acetazolamide is the only agent with a licence for Ménière disease
options.E: No diuretic is mentioned

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Hydrochlorothiazide plus triamterene
mcqs.explanation: A combination of hydrochlorothiazide and triamterene is the most commonly used medical treatment. Acetazolamide, furosemide, and spironolactone are also used by some.

sourceRefs.excerpt: A combination of hydrochlorothiazide and triamterene is the most commonly used medical treatment for Ménière’s disease.

mcqs.question: What effect does the review attribute to intratympanic steroids?

options.A: A calming effect, with fewer and less severe spells for up to 2 years
options.B: Immediate recovery of hearing to normal in all patients
options.C: They are useful in migraine but not in Ménière disease
options.D: They ablate vestibular function like gentamicin
options.E: They are given only intravenously

mcqs.correctAnswerText: A calming effect, with fewer and less severe spells for up to 2 years
mcqs.explanation: Intratympanic steroids have been noted to have a calming effect on Ménière ears. The number and severity of spells seem to decrease for up to 2 years.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Intratympanic steroids have been noted to have a calming effect on Ménière’s ears. 24 The number and severity of spells seem to decrease for up to 2 years after use.

mcqs.question: What vertigo-control result does the review cite for endolymphatic shunts and sac procedures?

options.A: Improvement in about two-thirds, similar to improvement in nonsurgical cases over time
options.B: Cure of hearing loss in 90%
options.C: Worse vertigo than the natural history in every series
options.D: These operations are no longer described
options.E: Benefit only in bilateral disease

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Improvement in about two-thirds, similar to improvement in nonsurgical cases over time
mcqs.explanation: Endolymphatic shunts, cochleosacculotomy, and sac decompression have been used for decades. Vertigo control improved in about two-thirds, similar to nonsurgical cases over time.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Improvement in vertigo control has been achieved in about two-thirds of treated patients. 29 This is similar to the improvement seen in nonsurgically treated cases over time.

mcqs.question: Which destructive options does the review name when the aim is to disconnect a failing labyrinth, and when are they usually avoided?

options.A: Gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy; usually avoided when disease is bilateral
options.B: Endolymphatic shunt as the only destructive operation
options.D: Sodium restriction is the destructive step
options.E: They are preferred in bilateral disease

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy; usually avoided when disease is bilateral
mcqs.explanation: The favoured destructive means named are gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy. Destructive procedures are not usually used in bilateral cases.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the favored means are destructive: gentamicin ablation, vestibular neurectomy, and labyrinthectomy. The rationale for these treatments is to functionally disconnect the labyrinth
